What are Bitcoin fees right now?

answer: A satoshi is the smallest unit of Bitcoin. One bitcoin is 100 million sats.
Bitcoin is digital money with a fixed supply of 21 million. No bank or government controls it.
Miners hash block data plus a nonce through SHA-256 until the result is low enough. It is a brute-force lottery, not a math puzzle.
The Lightning Network is a Bitcoin layer for instant, low-fee payments that settle on the main chain.
Self-custody means you hold the keys. Not your keys, not your coins: an exchange balance is someone else's promise.
A seed phrase is the backup word list that can restore a wallet. Never type it into a website or chat.
Proof of work makes adding blocks expensive in energy and hardware, so rewriting history is costly.

q: Why is the supply capped at 21 million?
answer: The protocol only allows 21 million bitcoin. The cap is enforced by nodes, not by a company.
A full node checks every block against the rules. Don't trust, verify.
The Bitcoin whitepaper is the 2008 paper by Satoshi Nakamoto that describes peer-to-peer electronic cash.
Time preference is how much you value spending now versus later. Sound money rewards waiting.
Dollar-cost averaging means buying a fixed amount on a schedule, instead of trying to time the market. Not financial advice.
A UTXO is an unspent transaction output. Bitcoin tracks those coins, not account balances.
Taproot is a Bitcoin upgrade that uses Schnorr signatures and makes complex spends look simpler.
Every 2016 blocks, Bitcoin retargets difficulty so blocks stay near ten minutes apart.
A transaction fee is what you pay miners, usually priced in satoshis per virtual byte.
Bitcoin was created by Satoshi Nakamoto, who published the whitepaper in 2008 and then stepped away.
The halving cuts the new-coin subsidy in half every 210,000 blocks, about every four years.

q: What does not your keys, not your coins mean?
answer: If someone else holds the keys, they control the bitcoin. Self-custody means the keys are yours.
The mempool is the set of valid transactions a node has seen but that are not in a block yet.
An address is a shareable destination derived from a key. The private key is what spends the coins.
Satoshi's Favor is the in-app hashing game. Points from quests, level-ups, and badges can open a mining window.

q: How do I earn XP on Bitcoin Quest?
answer: XP is experience in the app. Daily gains are full through 500, half through 900, then a quarter until the shared 1,000 cap.
Orange Tickets can enter the sats raffle. Draws are announced in Global Chat.
Quest Hub is where quizzes, trivia, polls, Flex, and Satoshi's Favor live.

q: How do I turn on two-factor auth?
answer: Open Settings and turn on an authenticator. This device can be remembered for 30 days. Sensitive changes still ask for a fresh code.
Orange Tickets are the shop currency. You can earn them from the daily spin, activity, and referrals.
The daily quiz is a short Bitcoin question in Quest Hub. The server checks the reward.

q: How do gifts work in the app?
answer: Gifts let you send an in-app gift to another member. Open the gifts page to send or receive one.
Proof of Walk connects a walk or run and can earn XP, with a daily cap.
